verses.text: In the four hundred and eightieth year after Israel left Egypt, Solomon began building the LORD's house. It was the fourth year of his reign over Israel, in Ziv, the second month.
The house King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
The porch at the front ran twenty cubits across the width of the building and extended ten cubits out from it.
Solomon made windows with fixed latticework for the house.
He built a structure with several floors against the walls all around the temple hall and inner sanctuary. He made rooms along the sides of the building.

The rooms on the lowest floor were five cubits wide, the middle ones six cubits wide, and the top ones seven cubits wide. He made ledges on the outside of the temple wall to support the beams without cutting into the walls.
The stone was cut at the quarry before it reached the building site. No hammer, ax, or other iron tool could be heard in the house while it was being built.
The entrance to the middle side rooms was on the right side of the house. Winding stairs led up to the middle floor and from there to the third.
Solomon built and finished the house, roofing it with cedar beams and planks.
He built the stories along the whole house, each five cubits high, and attached them to the house with cedar timbers.
The LORD gave Solomon this message:
“About this house you're building, if you follow my statutes, carry out my rulings, and keep all my commands, I'll keep the promise I made to your father David through you.
I'll live among the Israelites and never abandon my people Israel.”
So Solomon finished building the house.
He lined the inside walls with cedar boards from floor to ceiling and laid cypress boards on the floor.
At the back of the house he used cedar boards from floor to ceiling to build a room twenty cubits deep. He made it the inner sanctuary, the Most Holy Place.
The temple hall in front of the inner sanctuary was forty cubits long.
The cedar inside was carved with buds and open flowers. Cedar covered everything, so no stone could be seen.
Solomon prepared the inner sanctuary inside the house to hold the ark of the LORD's covenant.
The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He covered it with pure gold and covered the altar with cedar.
Solomon covered the inside of the house with pure gold. He stretched gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary and covered it with gold.
He continued until the whole house was covered in gold. He also covered the entire altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary with gold.
He made two cherubim out of olive wood for the inner sanctuary. Each stood ten cubits high.
Each wing of the first cherub measured five cubits. It was ten cubits across from one wingtip to the other.
The other cherub also measured ten cubits. Both cherubim had the same size and shape.
Each cherub stood ten cubits high.

He placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary with their wings stretched out. One touched the wall on one side, and the other touched the opposite wall. Their other wings met in the middle of the room.
He covered both cherubim with gold.
All around the walls of the house, in the inner and outer rooms, he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
He covered the floor with gold in both the inner and outer rooms.
For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made olive-wood doors. The lintel and doorposts took up a fifth of the wall.
He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers into the two olive-wood doors and covered them with gold, pressing the gold onto the carved cherubim and palm trees.
He also made olive-wood doorposts for the entrance to the temple hall. They took up a fourth of the wall.
He made two cypress doors, each with two folding panels.
He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers into the doors and fitted gold over the carvings.
He built the inner courtyard with three rows of cut stone and one row of cedar beams.
The builders laid the foundation of the LORD's house in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
In the eleventh year, in Bul, the eighth month, every part of the house was finished according to its plans. It took Solomon seven years to build it.
